exact code and decided it is safe, and here is the reason. The key is a fingerprint of the matched TEXT,
so EDITING that code invalidates the verdict and the hit resurfaces -- which is the point.
Rationale for each rule id lives in docs/SECURITY_PATTERN_SWEEP_2026-07.md.
Never clear a hit here without recording why in that document.

005d6a4b2834.why: Tenant-independent BY DESIGN, and tenant-scoping it would be the bug. This is the H2->Postgres whole-database promotion (Move 9 A4): it copies every row of every business table from source to target. A tenant predicate here would silently drop every other tenant's data during a migration. REG-94 triage, Move 11 Wave 0.1. (Re-added 2026-08-01 after an accidental git checkout -- lost the fingerprint though the code and reasoning are unchanged.)

The fail-open direction (empty map -> 'no override configured' -> the role's full declared ceiling applies) is deliberately the SAME as H4's reasoning one module over (IdentityRoleLookup.rolesFor, fingerprint ddbcb35ee7ee): the worst case of a lookup fault is identical to 'this admin never configured a runtime restriction here', which is exactly today's pre-C2 behavior for every app that hasn't adopted the feature -- never a widened grant, only a narrowing that fails to apply. RolePermissions' own ceiling intersection (a separate, independently-tested control) is what actually enforces 'never beyond the ceiling'; this lookup only ever supplies an optional narrowing on top of it.
